title: Palm Royale
synopsis: Palm Beach, 1969. The most exclusive ball of the season has one empty seat and you intend to fill it. Smile. Lie beautifully.

nodes.text: The Palm Royale's brass doors have turned away duchesses. You have a borrowed Pucci dress, forty-one dollars, and a smile you have practiced in three mirrors. The doorman lifts an eyebrow.

choices.text: Sweep past as if you own the place
choices.consequence: Confidence is a kind of credential.

choices.text: Slip in through the cabana service path
choices.consequence: Servants' doors are never watched the way front ones are.

choices.text: Produce a forged sponsor's letter
choices.consequence: Ink and audacity. A dangerous pairing.

nodes.text: Evelyn Rollins materializes like weather. "I don't know you," she says, which is the worst thing a person can be here. Her eyes catalog your shoes.

choices.text: Drop a name she can't check
choices.consequence: A dead countess is a wonderful alibi.

choices.text: Compliment her late husband's foundation
choices.consequence: Flattery aimed at the dead rarely misses.

nodes.text: The cabanas smell of coconut oil and money. A pool boy named Robert watches you not belong. He could shout. He doesn't.

choices.text: Tip him your last bill for silence
choices.consequence: Loyalty bought is loyalty, for an hour.

choices.text: Ask him who really runs this place
choices.consequence: The staff always knows where the bodies tan.

nodes.text: The membership secretary reads your letter twice. The signature is good. The letterhead is better. "Mrs. Donahue vouches for you?" she asks.

choices.text: Insist, warmly, that you're old friends
choices.consequence: The bigger the lie, the straighter the back.

choices.text: Pivot to a different sponsor entirely
choices.consequence: Never defend a lie you can simply replace.

nodes.text: By the bar you become someone with a yacht and a tragedy. People lean in. A widow named Norma watches you from her wheelchair, unblinking.

choices.text: Charm Norma directly
choices.consequence: She is the gate behind the gate.

choices.text: Avoid her and work the younger set
choices.consequence: The young are easier and poorer.

nodes.text: Evelyn, softened, lets slip that Norma keeps a card file of everyone's secrets. Whoever holds it holds the season. The file is upstairs.

choices.text: Plan to reach the file tonight
choices.consequence: Knowledge here is the only true currency.

choices.text: Decide the file is too dangerous to want
choices.consequence: Some doors are walls in disguise.

nodes.text: The bartender mixes a grasshopper and a warning. "They'll let you in," he says. "They just won't ever let you leave clean." He slides you a key. Cabana 9.

choices.text: Pocket the key
choices.consequence: Every key is a question you'll have to answer later.

choices.text: Refuse it and stay visible
choices.consequence: Suspicion loves the person who hides.

nodes.text: You are seated, somehow, at the good table. The conversation is a minefield of maiden names. Someone asks where you summered as a girl.

choices.text: Invent a lake nobody dares not to know
choices.consequence: Geography is forgiving to the bold.

choices.text: Turn the question back as a joke
choices.consequence: Deflection is its own elegance.

nodes.text: Robert finds you again. "Norma's nurse takes a smoke break at four," he says, and walks off whistling. He has decided you are interesting, which is its own danger.

choices.text: Time your move to four o'clock
choices.consequence: Schedules are the soft spots of fortresses.

choices.text: Win Norma over honestly instead
choices.consequence: The long way is sometimes the only safe way.

nodes.text: Models drift down a poolside runway in next year's clothes. Evelyn places a hand on your arm — friendly, or a leash, you can't tell. A photographer circles.

choices.text: Pose for the photographer
choices.consequence: A picture is proof, and proof cuts both ways.

choices.text: Slip out of frame
choices.consequence: The uncaptured are the uncatchable.

nodes.text: A woman named Dinah corners you with a smile like a paper cut. "I looked you up," she says. "Funny — you don't exist." She hasn't told anyone. Yet.

choices.text: Offer her something she wants
choices.consequence: Every rival is an ally who hasn't been paid.

choices.text: Threaten her with a bluff
choices.consequence: Show teeth and pray she doesn't count them.

nodes.text: Norma's grip is iron despite the chair. "You're a fraud," she says, almost fondly. "I was one too, once. It's exhausting, isn't it." She studies you like a daughter she might invent.

choices.text: Confess everything to her
choices.consequence: The truth, told to the right enemy, becomes armor.

choices.text: Deny it and hold your shape
choices.consequence: Never blink first at the queen.

nodes.text: Paddles rise for a diamond nobody needs. To bid is to be seen as somebody. To not bid is to be seen as nobody. You have forty-one dollars.

choices.text: Bid wildly on credit you don't have
choices.consequence: The chasm between seeming and being is one signature wide.

choices.text: Win the room without spending a cent
choices.consequence: The cleverest never open their purse.

nodes.text: Someone slips a card under your door. They know your real name, your real address, your real nothing. Meet under the banyan at midnight, it says, or be announced.

choices.text: Go to the banyan tree
choices.consequence: Blackmail is a conversation you're allowed to win.

choices.text: Burn the note and run the ball anyway
choices.consequence: Sometimes nerve is the only reply.

nodes.text: Evelyn's husband Skeet, half-asleep on Demerol and old money, takes a shine to you. His signature could open every account in Palm Beach. He offers you a pen.

choices.text: Take the pen and the access
choices.consequence: Power borrowed is power, until the lender wakes.

choices.text: Decline, gently, and keep his trust
choices.consequence: Restraint, here, looks almost like virtue.

nodes.text: Your story is fraying at the cuffs. Two women whisper behind their fans. The season can smell blood, and it is patient about dinner.

choices.text: Get ahead of the rumor with a bigger one
choices.consequence: Drown a small fire in a flood.

choices.text: Find an exit and an alibi
choices.consequence: Know the back stairs before you need them.

nodes.text: The ballroom is being strung with ten thousand lights for tomorrow's Beach Ball. You will be in this room. The only question left is as what.

choices.text: Plan to be crowned the season's hostess
choices.consequence: Aim at the throne or don't aim at all.

choices.text: Plan a quieter, safer triumph
choices.consequence: Survival can be its own kind of victory.

nodes.text: The press man has a photo of you slipping through the cabana door on day one. "Page six," he says, "or page nobody. Your choice, and your favor."

choices.text: Trade him a juicier secret
choices.consequence: Feed the wolf someone else's hand.

choices.text: Charm him into burying it
choices.consequence: Charm is cheaper than secrets and twice as fast.

nodes.text: The ballroom blazes. Every name you have borrowed and broken is here under one roof. Evelyn taps a glass. Norma watches from the dark edge, smiling at no one.

choices.text: Step into the light and take the floor
choices.consequence: The center of the room is where masks come off — or weld on.

choices.text: Work the margins and stay legible
choices.consequence: Let the spotlight find someone hungrier.

nodes.text: A glass is pressed into your hand and the room turns to you, expecting words. Whatever you say next becomes the truth about who you are here.

choices.text: Toast to the season and your new life
choices.consequence: Claim the lie out loud and watch it set like cement.

choices.text: Toast to Norma — and tell the truth
choices.consequence: Honesty, in a room of liars, is the loudest sound there is.

choices.text: Use the toast to expose the whole rotten club
choices.consequence: Burn it down and see who runs for the doors.

nodes.text: They are applauding. You did it. The orchestra swells and Robert, by the doors, gives you a small, sad nod — he, at least, remembers who walked in.

choices.text: Accept the crown and become Mrs. Palm Beach
choices.consequence: Some prisons have wonderful views.

choices.text: Walk out the front door, free and forty-one dollars richer
choices.consequence: The only way to win the game is to leave the table.

nodes.text: You marry the right name and bury the wrong one. For thirty years you reign over the Palm Royale, terrified every single morning that someone will remember the cabana door. Nobody ever does. That is the cruelest part.

Norma laughs until she coughs, then has them set you a permanent place at her table. "A fraud who admits it," she wheezes, "is just an honest woman with ambition." You are in. You are also, finally, yourself.

By dawn the columns are full of it — the affairs, the ledgers, the borrowed everything. The Palm Royale never recovers its shine. Neither do you, exactly, but you taught a roomful of queens that their crowns were rented too.

You leave the way they never expected — through the brass doors, into the salt night, owing no one a name. Behind you the lights blaze on for people who can never leave. Ahead of you, the dark is wide open.
